core.title: HyperLLM: Hypergraph-Enhanced Large Language Model for Remaining Useful Life Prediction
core.summary: 航空发动机退化过程复杂，多传感器信号强耦合，使剩余使用寿命预测面临信息提取困难。本文提出HyperLLM，以自适应超图及超图卷积提取空间退化特征，以退化感知时间嵌入捕捉时间特征，再通过轻量适配器融合，并利用任务嵌入提示适配冻结的大语言模型。摘要报告其在C-MAPSS与N-CMAPSS上具有较强预测精度和泛化能力，但未给出具体指标与对照结果。本解读仅依据摘要，适合用于判断方法相关性，不足以确认性能优势幅度。[摘要]

article.lead: 航空发动机退化过程复杂，多变量传感器信号又相互耦合，如何从中提取有效信息、预测剩余使用寿命？HyperLLM将超图建模与大语言模型结合，阅读价值在于理解它如何组织空间关联、时间退化与任务适配。

sections.title: 寿命预测的难点：退化复杂与信号耦合
paragraphs: 准确预测航空发动机的剩余使用寿命（RUL），对保障飞行安全具有重要意义。摘要指出，发动机退化过程复杂，难以准确建模；与此同时，多变量传感器信号存在较强耦合，阻碍退化信息的有效提取与利用。研究因此需要同时处理退化过程和信号之间的关联。
摘要将大语言模型的理解与推理能力视为建模复杂退化过程的新切入点。本文提出的超图增强方法，正是尝试把多源传感信息组织成可供大语言模型利用的退化表征。

sections.title: 空间与时间特征融合，再适配冻结的大模型
paragraphs: 方法首先构建自适应超图，融合多源退化信息，并通过超图卷积提取拓扑空间退化特征。与此同时，退化感知时间嵌入模块负责捕捉时间退化特征，随后利用轻量级适配器完成多维特征融合。
在融合表征的基础上，方法构建任务嵌入提示，引导大语言模型完成任务适配，同时保持其参数冻结。摘要将这一设计与保留大语言模型先验知识、增强预测性能联系起来，但未展开提示形式、适配器结构或具体训练配置。

paragraphs: 仅凭摘要，无法判断实验使用的样本规模、数据划分、比较基线，以及“泛化能力”对应的具体测试设置。也无法确认空间建模、时间嵌入、适配器与任务提示各自贡献了多少。这些属于摘要未报告的信息，并不意味着论文没有进行相应分析。

core.title: Optimizing Hip Joint Prosthetics through Integrated Design, Biomaterials, and Digital Manufacturing Techniques: Current Trends and Challenges
core.abstract: As the demand for total hip replacement (THR) has continued to rise worldwide, the THR has evolved from the first stainless steel-polyethylene THR in the 1960s to today’s systems with advanced biomaterials, optimized designs, and digital manufacturing to ensure a better longevity, biocompatibility, and patient function. This review aims to consolidate the existing trends and challenges in optimization of hip joint prosthetics, ranging from material improvements, integrated biomechanical design, and testing processes to the new computational and additive manufacturing methodologies. The evidence is collected from the following: Metallic and Ceramic Bearing Materials, Surface Engineering, In vitro and tribocorrosion testing (hip simulators, electrochemical techniques such as OCP, EIS, and polarization) and Computational tools (finite element analysis, machine learning). These include low-modulus β-type titanium alloys that have been developed to be less detrimental in terms of stress shielding than the conventionally used Ti-6Al-4V (114 GPa) with a Young’s modulus closer to that of the bone (≈19–30 GPa), such as TNZT (55–70 GPa) and Ti-33Nb-4Sn (~36 GPa), as well as data-driven pipelines for alloy design that predict Young’s modulus and suggest new alloys. Surface modifications (porous coatings, hydroxyapatite coatings, anodizing, bioactive coatings) increase the corrosion resistance and osseointegration; ceramics (alumina, zirconia, ZTA, and silicon nitride) have a high wear resistance and are biocompatible, although monolithic alumina is reported to have >90% survival at 10–20 years, but with continued concerns on brittleness. Integrated modeling demonstrates clinically relevant load transfer and contact mechanics including peaks in von Mises stress in the liner of 6.6 MPa and head contact pressure of up to 11.9 MPa. AI can enable personalization and inverse/generative design of porous lattices (target porosities 50–90%), improve 3D planning accuracy (+/−7 mm), reduce peak interface stress by 36.6%, and provide outcome prediction (e.g., CBCT-guided planning with 87% accuracy in predicting osseointegration) and intraoperative and postoperative decision making support through sensor-equipped implants and real-time models (e.g., LSTM). However, there are still some significant drawbacks such as long-term clinical validation, wear/corrosion and osteolysis due to debris production, the ability to limit the printing of multi-materials, variability of process parameters, which impacts the reproducibility of the process, and cost and scalability challenges. For the future, an interdisciplinary approach towards smart and monitored patient-specific implants as well as strong manufacturing quality control and clinically validated digital-twin frameworks will likely be required for further progress. Recent developments in sensor technology and real-time data collection promise to further improve the monitoring of implants, which will help in the early detection of complications and personalized post-operative care. Moreover, combining machine learning algorithms and clinical data can enable predictive maintenance and adaptive treatment strategies. On-going collaboration between material scientists, engineers and clinicians will be critical to help bring these advances to successful, patient-centred hip replacement solutions.

计算方法既用于分析载荷传递与接触力学，也用于数据驱动的合金设计：预测杨氏模量并提出新合金建议。综述还讨论了增材制造，以及人工智能支持的多孔晶格逆向设计和生成式设计。

core.title: From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.
core.abstract: Enzyme engineering has long relied on rational design and directed evolution, yet both remain bounded by natural enzyme space - a constraint felt acutely across the largely uncharacterised microbial world. The 2021 advent of accurate structure prediction marked an inflection point, catalysing AI methods that now extend far beyond folding. These tools are organism-agnostic; the microbial domain is their proving ground because it supplies both the uncharacterised sequence space and the expression hosts. Here we examine three stages: mining microbial sequence space; generative design, whether conditioned on structure or sequence; and machine learning-guided directed evolution. We trace the trajectory from reading the protein universe toward writing it, asking where each has delivered for microbial biocatalysis. Because published claims are hard to compare, we propose a tiered framework - catalysis, selectivity, producibility, process fit - for judging whether an AI-designed enzyme is a useful biocatalyst rather than merely a functional protein.

core.abstract: The steady functioning of power electronic-based systems is linked to fault localization and identification for converters, which is gaining a lot of attention. Artificial intelligence (AI), a representation of sophisticated algorithms is offering new solutions. This article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to diagnose open-circuit defects in power electronic converters, which are essential parts of contemporary power systems. From an algorithmic point of view, the fault diagnosis techniques are methodically classified and summarized encompassing a variety of approaches such as multimodal fusion, hybrid models, neural networks (such as convolutional and recurrent neural networks), and traditional machine learning (such as support vector machines and extreme learning machines). Their effectiveness is assessed in terms of real-time capabilities, computational efficiency, and noise robustness. Furthermore, future possibilities and suggested paths for AI-driven fault diagnosis are presented, promoting advancements to improve power converter systems' dependability and affordability. core.title: Research Progress in Machine-Learning-Based Fault Diagnosis for Mechanical Equipment
core.abstract: Fault diagnosis of mechanical equipment is essential for ensuring safe and reliable operation and reducing losses caused by unplanned downtime. With the large-scale deployment of sensors and the Industrial Internet of Things, condition-monitoring data have grown rapidly in both volume and dimensionality. Conventional diagnostic approaches that rely on human expertise and signal processing are increasingly inadequate, while machine learning, especially deep learning, has become the dominant research paradigm because of its automatic feature extraction and powerful nonlinear modeling capabilities. Following a data-feature-model-application framework, this paper systematically reviews advances in machine-learning applications for mechanical equipment fault diagnosis. It first outlines the basic diagnostic workflow, commonly used monitoring signals, and representative public datasets. It then reviews diagnostic methods based on conventional machine learning, including feature engineering, support vector machines, and ensemble learning, as well as deep-learning methods based on convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, autoencoders, attention mechanisms, and Transformers, comparing their principles, applicable conditions, strengths, and limitations. For real industrial environments, the paper focuses on emerging directions such as few-shot learning, transfer learning, multisensor fusion and graph neural networks, federated learning, and generative-adversarial-network-based data augmentation, and summarizes their applications to representative systems including rotating machinery, motors, computer numerical control machine tools, and pumps. Finally, current challenges are analyzed from the perspectives of data quality, model generalization, interpretability, and real-time edge deployment, and future trends involving physics-data integration, foundation models, and intelligent operation and maintenance are discussed. The analysis shows that the field is evolving from discriminative diagnosis dependent on large amounts of labeled data toward few-shot, cross-condition, interpretable, and deployable solutions. Data governance and engineering implementation will therefore become the principal bottlenecks constraining practical adoption.

core.title: Optimization of deep learning algorithms in automotive fault diagnosis systems
core.venue: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)
core.abstract: To address the issue of insufficient modeling efficiency of high-dimensional sensor data in the identification of complex equipment operating states, a deep learning diagnostic computing framework for automotive system operation signals is constructed. By designing a multilayer convolutional feature extraction network and a time-series dynamic modeling structure, high-dimensional feature representation and time-series dependency learning of multi-source sensor signals are achieved; further, an attention weight calculation mechanism is introduced to adaptively weight key features, thereby improving the stability and computational efficiency of diagnostic decisions. During the model training stage, cross-entropy loss and gradient optimization strategies are constructed, and the GPU parallel computing mechanism is used to enhance the efficiency of large-scale data processing. Experimental results show that under 15,000 sample data conditions, the diagnostic accuracy of this algorithm reaches 94.7%, and the training convergence speed is improved by approximately 18.3%.

papers.title: Optimizing Hip Joint Prosthetics through Integrated Design, Biomaterials, and Digital Manufacturing Techniques: Current Trends and Challenges
papers.abstract: As the demand for total hip replacement (THR) has continued to rise worldwide, the THR has evolved from the first stainless steel-polyethylene THR in the 1960s to today’s systems with advanced biomaterials, optimized designs, and digital manufacturing to ensure a better longevity, biocompatibility, and patient function. This review aims to consolidate the existing trends and challenges in optimization of hip joint prosthetics, ranging from material improvements, integrated biomechanical design, and testing processes to the new computational and additive manufacturing methodologies. The evidence is collected from the following: Metallic and Ceramic Bearing Materials, Surface Engineering, In vitro and tribocorrosion testing (hip simulators, electrochemical techniques such as OCP, EIS, and polarization) and Computational tools (finite element analysis, machine learning). These include low-modulus β-type titanium alloys that have been developed to be less detrimental in terms of stress shielding than the conventionally used Ti-6Al-4V (114 GPa) with a Young’s modulus closer to that of the bone (≈19–30 GPa), such as TNZT (55–70 GPa) and Ti-33Nb-4Sn (~36 GPa), as well as data-driven pipelines for alloy design that predict Young’s modulus and suggest new alloys. Surface modifications (porous coatings, hydroxyapatite coatings, anodizing, bioactive coatings) increase the corrosion resistance and osseointegration; ceramics (alumina, zirconia, ZTA, and silicon nitride) have a high wear resistance and are biocompatible, although monolithic alumina is reported to have >90% survival at 10–20 years, but with continued concerns on brittleness. Integrated modeling demonstrates clinically relevant load transfer and contact mechanics including peaks in von Mises stress in the liner of 6.6 MPa and head contact pressure of up to 11.9 MPa. AI can enable personalization and inverse/generative design of porous lattices (target porosities 50–90%), improve 3D planning accuracy (+/−7 mm), reduce peak interface stress by 36.6%, and provide outcome prediction (e.g., CBCT-guided planning with 87% accuracy in predicting osseointegration) and intraoperative and postoperative decision making support through sensor-equipped implants and real-time models (e.g., LSTM). However, there are still some significant drawbacks such as long-term clinical validation, wear/corrosion and osteolysis due to debris production, the ability to limit the printing of multi-materials, variability of process parameters, which impacts the reproducibility of the process, and cost and scalability challenges. For the future, an interdisciplinary approach towards smart and monitored patient-specific implants as well as strong manufacturing quality control and clinically validated digital-twin frameworks will likely be required for further progress. Recent developments in sensor technology and real-time data collection promise to further improve the monitoring of implants, which will help in the early detection of complications and personalized post-operative care. Moreover, combining machine learning algorithms and clinical data can enable predictive maintenance and adaptive treatment strategies. On-going collaboration between material scientists, engineers and clinicians will be critical to help bring these advances to successful, patient-centred hip replacement solutions.

papers.title: From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering has long relied on rational design and directed evolution, yet both remain bounded by natural enzyme space - a constraint felt acutely across the largely uncharacterised microbial world. The 2021 advent of accurate structure prediction marked an inflection point, catalysing AI methods that now extend far beyond folding. These tools are organism-agnostic; the microbial domain is their proving ground because it supplies both the uncharacterised sequence space and the expression hosts. Here we examine three stages: mining microbial sequence space; generative design, whether conditioned on structure or sequence; and machine learning-guided directed evolution. We trace the trajectory from reading the protein universe toward writing it, asking where each has delivered for microbial biocatalysis. Because published claims are hard to compare, we propose a tiered framework - catalysis, selectivity, producibility, process fit - for judging whether an AI-designed enzyme is a useful biocatalyst rather than merely a functional protein.

papers.abstract: The steady functioning of power electronic-based systems is linked to fault localization and identification for converters, which is gaining a lot of attention. Artificial intelligence (AI), a representation of sophisticated algorithms is offering new solutions. This article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to diagnose open-circuit defects in power electronic converters, which are essential parts of contemporary power systems. From an algorithmic point of view, the fault diagnosis techniques are methodically classified and summarized encompassing a variety of approaches such as multimodal fusion, hybrid models, neural networks (such as convolutional and recurrent neural networks), and traditional machine learning (such as support vector machines and extreme learning machines). Their effectiveness is assessed in terms of real-time capabilities, computational efficiency, and noise robustness. Furthermore, future possibilities and suggested paths for AI-driven fault diagnosis are presented, promoting advancements to improve power converter systems' dependability and affordability. papers.title: Research Progress in Machine-Learning-Based Fault Diagnosis for Mechanical Equipment
papers.abstract: Fault diagnosis of mechanical equipment is essential for ensuring safe and reliable operation and reducing losses caused by unplanned downtime. With the large-scale deployment of sensors and the Industrial Internet of Things, condition-monitoring data have grown rapidly in both volume and dimensionality. Conventional diagnostic approaches that rely on human expertise and signal processing are increasingly inadequate, while machine learning, especially deep learning, has become the dominant research paradigm because of its automatic feature extraction and powerful nonlinear modeling capabilities. Following a data-feature-model-application framework, this paper systematically reviews advances in machine-learning applications for mechanical equipment fault diagnosis. It first outlines the basic diagnostic workflow, commonly used monitoring signals, and representative public datasets. It then reviews diagnostic methods based on conventional machine learning, including feature engineering, support vector machines, and ensemble learning, as well as deep-learning methods based on convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, autoencoders, attention mechanisms, and Transformers, comparing their principles, applicable conditions, strengths, and limitations. For real industrial environments, the paper focuses on emerging directions such as few-shot learning, transfer learning, multisensor fusion and graph neural networks, federated learning, and generative-adversarial-network-based data augmentation, and summarizes their applications to representative systems including rotating machinery, motors, computer numerical control machine tools, and pumps. Finally, current challenges are analyzed from the perspectives of data quality, model generalization, interpretability, and real-time edge deployment, and future trends involving physics-data integration, foundation models, and intelligent operation and maintenance are discussed. The analysis shows that the field is evolving from discriminative diagnosis dependent on large amounts of labeled data toward few-shot, cross-condition, interpretable, and deployable solutions. Data governance and engineering implementation will therefore become the principal bottlenecks constraining practical adoption.

papers.title: Optimization of deep learning algorithms in automotive fault diagnosis systems
papers.venue: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)
papers.abstract: To address the issue of insufficient modeling efficiency of high-dimensional sensor data in the identification of complex equipment operating states, a deep learning diagnostic computing framework for automotive system operation signals is constructed. By designing a multilayer convolutional feature extraction network and a time-series dynamic modeling structure, high-dimensional feature representation and time-series dependency learning of multi-source sensor signals are achieved; further, an attention weight calculation mechanism is introduced to adaptively weight key features, thereby improving the stability and computational efficiency of diagnostic decisions. During the model training stage, cross-entropy loss and gradient optimization strategies are constructed, and the GPU parallel computing mechanism is used to enhance the efficiency of large-scale data processing. Experimental results show that under 15,000 sample data conditions, the diagnostic accuracy of this algorithm reaches 94.7%, and the training convergence speed is improved by approximately 18.3%.

摘要未交代比较基线、重复试验与不确定性，也未说明跨车辆、跨工况或实际部署的验证范围。因此，这些结果尚不足以判断模型的泛化能力和现场运行表现；这属于摘要的信息边界，不代表论文没有开展相关工作。
